'''Kwomtari''' is the eponymous language of the [[Kwomtari languages|Kwomtari family]] of [[Papua New Guinea]].

Spencer (2008) is a short grammar of Kwomtari. The language has an SOV{{clarify|date=August 2022}} constituent order and nominative–accusative alignment. Both subjects and objects are marked suffixally on the verb. Verbs are inflected for status (mood) rather than for tense or aspect.<ref>{{cite book | first = Katharine | last = Spencer | year = 2008 | chapter = Kwomtari grammar essentials | editor = Murray Honsberger, Carol Honsberger and Ian Tupper | title = Kwomtari phonology and grammar essentials | location = Ukarumpa, Papua New Guinea | publisher = SIL-PNG Academic Publications | pages = 53–180 | isbn = 978-9980-0-3426-7}}</ref>

==Locations==
Ethnologue lists Kwomtari as spoken in six villages in Komtari (Kwomtari) ward ({{coord|-3.596084|141.361577|type:city_region:PG|name=Kwomtari}}), [[Amanab Rural LLG]], [[Sandaun Province]].<ref name="Ethnologue22-PNG">{{cite web |url=https://www.ethnologue.com/country/PG/languages |title=Papua New Guinea languages |work=[[Ethnologue]]: Languages of the World |edition=22nd |editor1-last=Eberhard |editor1-first=David M. |editor2-last=Simons |editor2-first=Gary F. |editor3-last=Fennig |editor3-first=Charles D. |date=2019 |location=Dallas |publisher=[[SIL International]]}}</ref><ref name="UN-PNG">{{cite web |url=https://data.humdata.org/dataset/village-coordinates-lookup |title=Papua New Guinea Village Coordinates Lookup |author=United Nations in Papua New Guinea |work=Humanitarian Data Exchange |version=1.31.9 |date=2018}}</ref>

Baron (2007) lists Kwomtari-speaking villages as Mango, Kwomtari, Baiberi, Yenabi, Yau'uri, and Wagroni.<ref name="Baron-Kwomtari">{{cite web |url=http://www.kwomtari.net/ |title=The Kwomtari Phylum |last=Baron |first=Wietze |date=October 2007 |accessdate=2019-09-22}}</ref>

The phoneme {{IPA|/ɸ/}} is realized as a voiced bilabial fricative {{IPA|[β]}} intervocalically and voiceless bilabial fricative {{IPA|[ɸ]}} elsewhere. The realization of the phoneme {{IPA|/ɭ/}} is in free variation between a voiced retroflex lateral {{IPA|[ɭ]}} and a voiced retroflex stop {{IPA|[ɖ]}}.

The unusual vowel phonemes {{IPA|/i̞/}} and {{IPA|/u̞/}} are of intermediate height between cardinal {{IPA|[i]/[u]}} and {{IPA|[e]/[o]}} respectively but without the centralization present in {{IPA|[ɪ]}} and {{IPA|[ʊ]}}. They have also been attested in [[weri language|Weri]], a [[Goilalan languages|Goilalan]] language of south-east Papua, and certain [[Dani languages|Dani]] dialects.<ref>Foley (1986:54)</ref>
